I farm small land, so I do not spread myself too thin. I will keep most of my 7.7 mu in the wheat-maize system because that is what fits my land, my labor, and my irrigation well best. I will keep a smaller piece in cotton so I still have some cash-crop income, but I will not expand it too much because cotton takes more field watching and more pesticide work. I make steady decisions, not aggressive ones. At my age, after 45 years farming, I care more about avoiding a bad year than chasing the highest possible yield.

For wheat, I will use improved seed, put in moderate fertilizer, irrigate at the key times, and manage weeds and disease with a small number of sprays. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant hybrid maize on the same land because that double-cropping pattern is still the backbone of my farm. For maize, I will keep the stand strong, use enough nitrogen to support grain filling, and rely on one or two irrigations depending on rainfall. For cotton, I will keep it on a smaller area, use a bit more balanced potassium, and accept more pesticide passes because insects are usually the bigger problem there. I will use methods that save labor where I can, especially rotary tillage or no-tillage for the wheat-maize land, because I want the work to stay manageable for my household.
